newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israel blasts wound 13, Arab militants blamed.
newsitem.headline: Two Israel blasts wound 13, Arab militants blamed.

text.p: Two bomb blasts that Israel blamed on Arab militants wounded at least 13 people near Tel Aviv's central bus station on Thursday, officials said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the bombings bore the hallmark of Palestinian "terrorist" attacks and vowed to respond with "extreme severity".

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the explosions, which came against the backdrop of U.S.-brokered talks on Israel's long-delayed withdrawal from most of the West Bank city of Hebron.

"If it becomes clear that the terrorists who carried out this attack came from the Palestinian Authority (area), we will respond with extreme severity," Netanyahu told reporters after visiting wounded in a Tel Aviv hospital.
"According to all the signs, it appears to be a terrorist attack," he said.
National Police Chief Assaf Hefetz said the bombs were packed with nails and blew up 10 minutes and several metres (yards) apart. One Arab suspect was arrested, police said.

A spokeswoman for Tel Aviv's Ichilov hospital said 10 people were hurt, none seriously. The Magen David Adom ambulance service said three other people who were slightly wounded were taken to another hospital.

Moslem militant groups had vowed to avenge last week's shooting attack in Hebron by an off-duty Israeli soldier who wounded seven Palestinians in what he said was an attempt to stop Israel from carrying out its long-overdue troop redeployment.
Palestinian militants last mounted a bombing campaign in Israel in February and March last year when suicide bombers killed 59 people.

The militant Hamas group said at the time it was avenging the death of its master bomb-maker known as "The Engineer", Yahya Ayyash, who was killed in the Gaza Strip on January 5, 1996 by an exploding cellular telephone. Hamas blamed his assassination on Israel.
Hamas last carried out a bombing in Tel Aviv on March 4, 1996 killing 13 people at a busy shopping mall.
Kahalani said Thursday's bombs were planted in rubbish bins next to a cinema that screens sex movies.
"There was a very strong explosion under the Central Cinema, in a snack bar. A few minutes later, there was another blast," a witness told Army Radio.

"It was a tremendous explosion. A sunflower seed seller was hurt. Police arrived five minutes later. As they were checking things, another bomb went off and a policeman was hurt," said another witness.
The site is a run-down area of Tel Aviv that serves as an outdoor annex of the city's main enclosed central bus station situated several blocks away.
Shops were still open at the time of the blasts, at around 8:25 p.m. (1825 GMT).
